name: Ridge Rider Campground
note: Roadville-run campground on 220 wooded acres near the Potomac and Green Ridge State Forest; pull-through and back-in gravel sites with 30/50-amp and water for short stays (full hookups are the seasonal sites), cabins, tent sites; pool, camp store, propane, laundry. Large seasonal-camper section. Reservable online. RV sites from $43/night for 2 adults (quoted June 2027). RV Life 4*/$$$ ~$49/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude
inclusion_evidence: roadville.com/ridge-rider RV-sites page: transient pull-through/back-in 30/50A water+electric sites for RVs of all sizes, Newbook online booking; Newbook live quote Wed 2027-06-16, 2 adults, 23-ft trailer: RV sites from $43.26/night -> real transient RV campground (seasonal section alongside, not predominant for bookable stock); published base $43 (2026 quote) <= $50

lead.candidate_sites: creekside pop-up/tent spots per the operator
lead.note: RV loops sit on the hillside N of the road; the creek runs along the road below. Operator says creekside spots suit pop-ups, not RV sites.

name: Hillcrest River Campground
note: Open grassy hilltop campground 1/10 mile off I-68 exit 45 east of Cumberland; 60 RV/tent sites, full hookups on request (+$10/day, paid on arrival), dump station, flush toilets and hot shower in season, 24/7 convenience store next door, hiking trails and a decorative pond (no fishing). Same host runs the primitive Canal Tunnel River campground on the North Branch Potomac 3 miles away. Booked through Hipcamp only: $35/night for up to 4 plus $10 for hookups (2026). Hipcamp 95% over 174 reviews. RV Life 4.5*/$$$ ~$42/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude
inclusion_evidence: Hipcamp listing (active, instant-book, staff-verified, 174 reviews): 60 drive-in RV/tent sites for motor homes and trailers on open grass, FHU +$10/day, dump station, showers -> real transient RV campground; published base $35 + $10 hookups = $45 (2026) <= $50. Only other web presence is pinecliffresort.net, a content farm, deliberately not cited.

lead.note: hilltop field beside I-68 exit 45; only water is a small no-fishing pond at the S edge; Potomac frontage belongs to the separate Canal Tunnel River site
